title: Offline-First Mobile Inspection Engine in React Native with WatermelonDB SQLite & Idempotent Delta Sync
problem: Mobile applications for field agents (insurance surveyors, equipment inspectors, and logistics personnel) suffer from frozen user interfaces and catastrophic data loss when operating in basements, rural regions, or cellular dead zones. Standard mobile architectures relying on synchronous REST calls fail completely without internet access, while naive local caching strategies overwrite remote changes during bulk reconnection syncs. This project builds a production-grade offline-first mobile inspection engine in TypeScript using React Native and WatermelonDB. The system persists complex relational inspection records locally in SQLite, executes optimistic UI mutations with sub-15ms local commit times, synchronizes differential delta vectors with a Node.js backend using idempotent transactions, and deterministically resolves concurrent field edits using column-level Last-Write-Wins (LWW) timestamps.

use_cases.title: Aviation Runway & Aircraft Maintenance Logging
use_cases.first_sentence: Aircraft maintenance engineers conducting pre-flight checks inside shielded airport hangars frequently lose cellular and Wi-Fi connectivity.
use_cases.second_sentence: The mobile app records structural component wear measurements locally in SQLite, synchronizing delta updates to airline maintenance servers once the tablet reconnects.

use_cases.title: Insurance Property Damage Claims Assessment
use_cases.first_sentence: Insurance field claims adjusters assessing remote flood or hurricane damage sites must log detailed property estimates without active cell towers.
use_cases.second_sentence: The surveyor captures inspection items and estimated repair costs locally, automatically queuing updates that flush to the claims processing backend upon network reconnection.

use_cases.title: Commercial Cold-Storage Logistics Inventory Auditing
use_cases.first_sentence: Warehouse auditors working inside heavily insulated refrigerated facilities need continuous mobile checklist performance without network latency.
use_cases.second_sentence: The mobile client provides instantaneous UI state transitions using local WatermelonDB queries, synchronizing inventory count reconciliations upon exiting the refrigerated vault.

hard_parts: Configuring WatermelonDB reactive observable queries over SQLite to maintain 60 FPS scrolling across 5,000 cached records on mobile devices
Designing an idempotent differential synchronization protocol that tracks created, updated, and deleted record IDs with server-assigned sync timestamps
Resolving concurrent multi-device editing conflicts deterministically without overwriting unrelated fields in the same inspection entity
Managing background sync retries with exponential backoff and jitter to prevent thundering herd spikes during intermittent connection flapping
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating React Native UI views, WatermelonDB SQLite schema models, sync protocol clients, and Redux state slices
Mobile performance report proving sub-15ms local SQLite write latency and zero UI freeze across 5,000 local records

Anti-fake verification script simulating an airplane mode network cutoff, editing an inspection record locally, modifying the same record on the backend, reconnecting, and asserting non-conflicting field merge

architecture.data_flow: The field agent updates an inspection item on the React Native UI; WatermelonDB writes the mutation to SQLite in < 15ms and sets the record sync_status to 'updated'; the UI updates instantly via reactive observables; Redux Toolkit monitors NetInfo network status; when network connectivity is detected, the sync manager triggers a push/pull transaction with Node.js; the client sends local deltas since last_pulled_at; the Node.js server applies non-conflicting fields, resolves concurrent edits using column-level timestamps, commits to database, and returns server changes; the client applies server deltas to SQLite and updates last_pulled_at.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Server-side monotonically increasing sync sequence numbers and UUID v4 idempotency keys preventing duplicate record creation.

riskiest_component.name: Database Schema Desynchronization and Unresolvable Merge Conflicts

riskiest_component.fallback: Server-side conflict archive table preserving conflicting payloads for manual auditor review.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an offline-first mobile inspection engine in TypeScript with React Native, WatermelonDB SQLite, and Node.js differential sync.
worksheet.q2: Target users: mobile software engineers (React Native), frontend systems architects, and full-stack mobile developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: aviation runway maintenance logging, insurance property claims assessment, and cold-storage logistics auditing.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: WatermelonDB SQLite reactive queries, idempotent differential delta sync, multi-device column-level conflict resolution, and network retry backoff.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: React Native scaffolding, WatermelonDB models, Node.js sync server, and multi-client test suite. Synthetic inspection records only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero app store licenses. Fallback: in-memory SQLite store.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: database schema desynchronization and unresolvable merge conflicts. Fallback: strict migration versions and conflict audit archives.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: standard mobile app without real offline persistence. Anti-fake check 5 simulates two partitioned offline clients editing the same record and asserts deterministic merge.
worksheet.q10: Safe; synthetic equipment inspection data and local test servers only, zero personal data.
